scope: Post-freeze public-release review findings for Manager 4.17.12

defects.title: Pre-dispatch compatibility-shadow reconciliation blocks target-driven recovery before action dispatch
defects.preconditions: Multi-Hub registry is active; the selected old active Hub is structurally resolvable; both its per-instance and compatibility CURRENT checkpoints are missing/corrupt; another healthy registered target exists or the invocation is Manager-global.
defects.bad_behavior: Early registry resolution can mark registry mode active without proving compatibility CURRENT health. Top-level startup then unconditionally invokes compatibility-shadow reconciliation before action dispatch for every non-Doctor action. A real 53-scenario process-entry matrix proved that CURRENT missing/corrupt blocks exactly ListInstances, SwitchInstanceId, BindInstancePath, UpdateManager, BuildDistribution, BuildRelease and BuildAIContext before their action bodies. Doctor and Hub/context-bound operations retain their intended diagnostic/fail-closed behavior.
defects.root_cause: The system proved recovery at function/UI boundaries but did not execute the complete process-entry -> early resolution -> compatibility handling -> action gating -> dispatch path for degraded active-CURRENT states. The engineering state model also lacked an explicit active-Hub-valid / active-CURRENT-invalid state. This repeats the composition/reachability pattern already documented by MGR-DEF-0023, MGR-DEF-0024 and MGR-DEF-0026.

evidence.id: 53 executed; 14 product-contract failures; harness_error=false; failures are CURRENT missing/corrupt x List/Switch/Bind/UpdateManager/BuildDistribution/BuildRelease/BuildAIContext
